awarded.label: STRONG

awarded.title: Invalid validation allows users to unlock early
awarded.label: SAME_AREA

awarded.title: Missing disapproval check in `LockManager.sol::approveUSDPrice` allows simultaneous approval and disapproval of a price proposal
awarded.label: STRONG

awarded.title: When `LockManager.lockOnBehalf` is called from `MigrationManager`, the user's `reminder` will be set to 0, resulting in fewer received `MunchableNFTs`
awarded.label: SAME_AREA

awarded.title: Players can gain more NFTs benefiting from that past remainder in subsequent locks
awarded.label: SAME_AREA

awarded.title: User's schnibbles rewards are not harvested in the `setLockDuration` function
awarded.label: SUBSYSTEM_ONLY

candidates.title: LockManager.lockOnBehalf: anyone can extend a victim's unlockTime via a dust deposit (lock griefing)
candidates.description: lockOnBehalf(token, quantity, _onBehalfOf) credits the lock to _onBehalfOf but _lock() unconditionally sets lockedToken.unlockTime = block.timestamp + _lockDuration, where _lockDuration is the VICTIM's playerSettings.lockDuration (or lockdrop.minLockDuration). An attacker can call lockOnBehalf(token, 1 wei, victim) to push the victim's unlockTime forward to now + their duration, re-locking funds that were about to unlock. Unlike setLockDuration (which has LockDurationReducedError protection), _lock has no guard against extending an existing lock, so the griefing is repeatable and cheap.

candidates.title: AccountManager.addSubAccount: anyone can claim an arbitrary unregistered address as a sub-account, blocking its lock
candidates.description: addSubAccount(_subAccount) only requires _subAccount to be unregistered with mainAccounts[_subAccount]==0; there is no consent from _subAccount. An attacker claims a victim address as their sub-account, setting mainAccounts[victim]=attacker. LockManager._lock calls accountManager.getPlayer(recipient) and reverts SubAccountCannotLockError if the resolved main account != recipient, so the victim cannot lock on their own behalf until they call register() (which unlinks). This is a griefing/denial lever and pollutes the account graph.

candidates.title: LockManager USD price voting: a price feed that disapproved can also approve the same proposal (no cross-check)
candidates.description: approveUSDPrice only checks approvals[msg.sender]==_usdProposalId (already approved) but NOT disapprovals[msg.sender]; disapproveUSDPrice checks both. So a PriceFeed role that has already disapproved can still call approveUSDPrice, incrementing approvalsCount toward APPROVE_THRESHOLD while their disapproval also stands. This lets a single feed contribute to both tallies and can skew threshold-based execution of a price update.

candidates.title: MigrationManager.migrateAllNFTs / burnNFTs are permissionless with a caller-chosen _skip (batch ordering griefing)
candidates.description: migrateAllNFTs(_user,_skip) and burnNFTs(_user,_skip) are callable by anyone once the user has selected a lock action, and process a window [_skip, _skip+5). A griefer can call them with chosen _skip values to control which 5-token window is processed first / leave gaps, complicating the user's migration accounting and emitting confusing partial events. Combined with the per-snapshot `claimed` flag the end state is consistent, but the externally-driven batch boundaries are an availability/UX hazard.

candidates.title: LockManager.unlock does not recompute remainder; getLockedWeightedValue underflows if a token is configured with decimals > 18
candidates.description: unlock() decrements lockedToken.quantity but never adjusts lockedToken.remainder, so the NFT-cost remainder can become stale relative to the remaining quantity. Separately getLockedWeightedValue computes 10 ** (18 - decimals); a token configured with decimals > 18 underflows and reverts (0.8.25 checked math), bricking weighted-value/harvest reads for all players if such a token is ever configured.
